FDA Initiates Labeling Changes for GLP-1s Due to Rare But Serious Eye Disease Risk

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 consumers have a newly introduced symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.
  • It has been revealed that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S.
  • A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 consumers have a newly introduced symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

It has been revealed that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint said.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

The study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

In a 2024 podcast, Rizzo stated he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

It has been revealed that about 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 owners “challenging” to interpret.

Across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint mentioned patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint stated that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

As of publication, the FDA’s online label database did not yet show the latest warning on the drugs’ labels.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the recall covers some 2013 Acura RDX, ILX, Honda CR-V, Civic, and Accord models.
  • Industry observers note that the NHTSA documents show that the affected vehicles are equipped with airbag inflators that use a phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate propellant, which is intended to control moisture within the inflator.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that somehow, after all these years, there are still a considerable number of vehicles equipped with Takata airbags, though their number should be considerably lower in the near future. Honda just issued a recall for 810,592 cars equipped with Takata airbags that could rupture due to propellant degradation caused by high humidity.

According to documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the recall covers some 2013 Acura RDX, ILX, Honda CR-V, Civic, and Accord models. The affected Accords and Acuras are all from the 2013 model year, while the CR-V and Civic populations include both 2012 and 2013 vehicles.

See all results for used cars for sale near 11385.

Industry observers note that the NHTSA documents show that the affected vehicles are equipped with airbag inflators that use a phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate propellant, which is intended to control moisture within the inflator. Over time, exposure to high humidity and repeated temperature changes can cause the inflator to become brittle. When the brittle inflators are deployed, they could turn into projectiles that shoot metal fragments through the cabin, potentially injuring or killing occupants.

The recall comes after years of investigation and analysis by Honda, which was routinely shared with NHTSA. The recall documents show that on November 19, 2026, Honda determined that the inflators posed enough of a risk to warrant the latest recall.

Owners of affected models will be contacted by mail and urged to bring their vehicle to a Honda or Acura dealership. Dealer technicians will replace the driver and passenger airbag inflators with a different model for free. Dealers have already been notified of the recall, with owner notification letters scheduled to be sent on December 18. Owners concerned that their car might be included in the recall can check on the NHTSA recalls site as well as NHTSA’s dedicated Takata airbag recall page.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that battlefield 6 is about to receive a latest upgrade.
  • That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.
  • According to recent reports, thew newly introduced content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that battlefield 6 is about to receive a latest upgrade. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

According to recent reports, thew newly introduced content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this enhancement is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a massive pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Industry observers note that some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this revision is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

It has been revealed that speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Recent findings suggest that something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an revision. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Series production of the upcoming iX4 is officially underway at BMW Group’s manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary.
  • The iX4 is the second fully electric BMW model built at the facility, following the record-breaking production ramp-up of the new iX3 SUV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BMW’s fresh iX4 is almost here, and it could make range anxiety a thing of the past. With 428 miles of EPA range, more than 500 miles on the WLTP cycle, and ultra-fast charging, the new EV could make road trips a whole lot easier.

Series production of the upcoming iX4 is officially underway at BMW Group’s manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary.

The iX4 is the second fully electric BMW model built at the facility, following the record-breaking production ramp-up of the new iX3 SUV.

BMW said the plant began series production of an entirely upcoming model in less than two months after the tech giant introduced a 24-hour, three-shift schedule to ramp up output to meet higher-than-expected demand.

The latest iX4 will go on sale in March 2027 as an all-electric replacement for the X4. It will be available in two variants: the BMW iX4 50 xDrive and BMW iX4 40 xDrive, with a range-topping M60 xDrive set to follow shortly after.

It has been revealed that both versions use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The iX4 50 xDrive provides a combined 468 hp and 475 lb-ft of torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds.

The performance M60 version delivers a combined 603 hp and 645 lb-ft of torque, which BMW says is good for a 0 to 60 mph sprint in just 3.9 seconds.

Sources indicate that the iX4 features a distinct coupe-SUV-like silhouette rather than the traditional boxy, upright SUV design of the iX3. With a rakish roofline and an aerodynamic design, the new iX4 has a drag coefficient of just 0.23.

Like the iX3, the iX4 is based on BMW’s Neue Klasse architecture with its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system.

In a recent development, while EPA figures have yet to be finalized, BMW noted the upcoming iX4 has an estimated driving range of up to 428 miles on a single charge using a 112.2 kWh battery. Under WLTP conditions, it offers an all-electric range of up to 514 miles (828 km).

Sources indicate that thanks to its 800V architecture, BMW’s newly introduced iX4 can add up to 184 miles of range (384 km on the WLTP cycle) in just 10 minutes with charging speeds of up to 400 kW. Charging the vehicle from 10% to 80% takes about 21 minutes.

Like BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, the new iX4 features its updated interior design. The setup includes a large 17.9″ infotainment screen and BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a 42″ display spanning the base of the windshield.

Would Electrek consider adding a small “Markets” box at the top of each article, with checkmarks next to the regions the news applies to (North America, Europe, China, etc.)? It would make it easy to see at a glance whether a vehicle or announcement applies to your market without having to dig through the article for a mention in the last paragraph.

Recent findings suggest that the iX4 is 188.3″ long, 74.6″ wide, and 63.3″ tall, with a 114.1″ wheelbase, which is about the same size as the iX3. However, it’s slightly lower than the iX3 thanks to the sloped roofline.

Like all Gen6 BMW models, the fresh iX4 supports bidirectional charging, enabling it to be used as a mobile power source for e-bikes, camping equipment, or other electrical devices.

The new BMW iX4 50 xDrive will go on sale in March 2027, starting at $66,300, or $4,800 more than the iX3 50 xDrive. That doesn’t include the $1,495 destination fee.

In Germany, the latest BMW iX4 40 xDrive starts at €70,900 ($77,500), and in the UK it’s priced from £53,250 ($69,500), OTR.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know if I believe in the Bigfoot theory, but the tracks were right there,” an 87-year-old resident of Sanders County, Montana, told his local newspaper in 2003 after discovering some suspicious footprints.
  • Recent findings suggest that another file also focuses on purported cryptid tracks in the summer of 1982.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Forest Service has quietly published a handful of documents related to multiple, decades’ old Bigfoot sightings. While the files uploaded to the agency’s Freedom of Information Act online reading room may not offer definitive proof of the cryptid’s existence, they may help redirect unwanted political conversations at the Thanksgiving table this year.

Recent findings suggest that “I don’t know if I believe in the Bigfoot theory, but the tracks were right there,” an 87-year-old resident of Sanders County, Montana, told his local newspaper in 2003 after discovering some suspicious footprints. “What else could it be?”.

Recent findings suggest that another file also focuses on purported cryptid tracks in the summer of 1982. In that case, park rangers were actually dispatched to obtain plaster molds of footprints reported in Oregon’s Umatilla National Forest.Unfortunately, resource staffer Roger Baker didn’t sound impressed by what he found on June 17, 1982.

“It is my opinion that the tracks…were made by something other than a 300-pound-plus, two footed being,” Baker explained, although he did concede that the prints appeared “very natural.”.

The final archival document is a local resident’s somewhat rambling personal account of the history of Petty Creek, a forested area located about 30 miles west of Missoula, Montana. Among stories of ill-fated gold prospectors, camel importation, and buried treasure, Leo Kinney tells of his own near-brush with Bigfoot. According to Kinney, he and some fellow hunters didn’t actually see the hairy biped walking around, but they saw evidence of its recent presence.

“Tracks, a strong odor, and grunting were observed,” he wrote in 1980.

The U.S. Forestry Service’s archival uploads are fun reads, but many Sasquatch believers are still reeling from the recent release of Capturing Bigfoot. Released in October, the critically acclaimed documentary delves into the story behind the Patterson–Gimlin tape. The controversial home video recording is widely considered the most famous Bigfoot sighting of all time, although the film essentially confirms once-and-for-all that the grainy footage was a carefully constructed hoax.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to.
  • It has been revealed that recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to. Consider the feelings that come up for you when you think about it. Is it excitement about seeing the people you love? Is it dread at the anticipation of planning, conflict, or grief? For some, it’s all of the above.

It has been revealed that recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S. adults report holiday stressors (APA, 2023). Tensions arise due to finances, family conflict, grief, and other factors. Stress takes away from the pleasurable aspects of the season, which should include reconnection and rest.

Industry observers note that sometimes that is easier said than done. Here are 5 things we're saying no to this holiday season and strategies to achieve the happy holidays we deserve.

Sometimes that family holiday announcement sounds like a demand rather than an invitation. “Dinner is at 4 pm sharp. See you there!” Everyone assumes you’ll be there, and no one asks questions. They don’t ask if you can take time off work, afford the trip, or have other prepares. You feel obligated to attend despite any barriers you are facing.

Recent findings suggest that almost no one will tell you that you are allowed to consider your own needs before you RSVP yes. Ask yourself whether you have the time, energy, and money to participate this year. If the answer is no, it’s alright. Your family may be disappointed, and you may feel a little guilty, but it’s worth asking which will weigh on you more: the guilt of saying no or the cost of saying yes.

In toxic families, it’s the once-over as soon as you enter the room. Before you’ve even had a chance to sit down, someone has made a joke about your weight or graying hair, offered a backhanded compliment about the dish you contributed, or slipped in a dig about your personal life.

In a recent development, you may feel hurt, sad, or even angry, and you don’t have to ignore those feelings to preserve the holiday spirit. You can be silent and stone-faced to let the “joke” fall flat. You might excuse yourself and regroup in another room. If you want to address it directly and call out the hidden meaning, you can say, “That felt like a dig,” or ask, “What do you mean by that?” What you don’t have to do is tolerate disrespect.

In a recent development, when you want everyone to feel loved, it’s easy to slip into spending more than you intended. If you’ve ever hosted a large family gathering, you know how rapidly the groceries and gifts add up. And if you’re the one who hosts every year, it can feel like the work and the bill are yours by default.

Recent findings suggest that before you do anything, set a budget. Then share the work in ways that play into everyone’s strengths. Maybe enlist the nephew who can roast meat or the cousin who loves to bake, and assign cleanup to the one you prefer to stay out of the kitchen. Suggest rotating hosting duties. Do a gift exchange rather than buying individual gifts for everyone. You can show your love to your family with limits.

In some families, playing the dutiful daughter (or son) means everyone assumes you’ll make the holidays happen. Often it’s the family matriarch or the eldest daughter who initiates the first call about the holiday plans and is the one still in the kitchen long after everyone else has gone home. She is the family “glue” who keeps track of the invites, remembers who can’t eat what, and figures out where to seat the relatives who aren’t speaking. By the time the holiday arrives, she’s too tired to enjoy the fruits of her labor.

Recent findings suggest that if that sounds like you, name it. People who have never hosted may not realize all of the hidden effort that goes into an event. Bring it to their attention. Set limits on what you will do and ask for help, but don’t micromanage. If the person assigned to bring the rolls forgets, skip the rolls this year. If no one steps up, step back anyway. Initiative a smaller, more intimate gathering that won’t leave you frazzled at the end of it.

Sources indicate that the holidays aren’t the same after you’ve lost a loved one, and the first holiday season after a loss can be especially difficult. Family traditions may be upended. The person who always hosted and made everyone’s favorite dish is gone. Tensions that surface after the loss may still be hanging in the air.

According to recent reports, take a moment to evaluate your feelings. Ask yourself what you feel up to this year. Maybe it’s not the year to take on hosting duties, or perhaps you stop by for dessert rather than staying the entire day. You can choose to honor your loved one by retaining old traditions or step into the next chapter with fresh traditions in their memory. You can miss someone deeply and still make room for moments of joy this holiday season.

It has been revealed that it might seem strange that saying no could be the start of a happy holiday. The beauty is that you get to decide what a happy holiday looks like for you, and that it can change from year to year. Ask yourself what would make the holidays feel good to you this year and do it.

1 in 3 Infants Diagnosed With Peanut Allergy May Not Have the Condition

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, new research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, new research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

Industry observers note that A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

It has been revealed that researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

Sources indicate that among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, Newly introduced York, remarked these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

In a recent development, banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more promptly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s important for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she said.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

In a recent development, “The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

Clam discovered living inside of a sea urchin’s throat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the fact that a upcoming clam species (Vaticinaria gulicola) was discovered where the sun does not shine may be the least interesting thing about this bivalve.
  • Sources indicate that an international team of scientists conducting a deep-sea survey of the Great Australian Bight discovered the clam.
  • It has been revealed that they found V.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the fact that a upcoming clam species (Vaticinaria gulicola) was discovered where the sun does not shine may be the least interesting thing about this bivalve. V. gulicola lives inside of a deep-sea urchin. The clam appears to have made a little home for itself inside the urchin’s oesophagus, the tube that runs through the center of the urchin’s body and into the intestine. A study recently published in the journal ZooKeys details this highly unusual partnership.

Sources indicate that an international team of scientists conducting a deep-sea survey of the Great Australian Bight discovered the clam. The survey studied the seafloor at depths of 656 to 16,404 feet deep and uncovered 66,721 invertebrates representing 1,267 species. About a third of these species are believed to be upcoming to science—including this quirky clam.

It has been revealed that they found V. gulicola along the abyssal seafloor at depths of about 13,000 to 16,400 feet. At this depth, sunlight cannot penetrate the water column. During these deep trawls, the team found clams equipped with threads for attaching to a host, but did not see any hosts. Additional searching revealed more clams lodged inside thin, slippery tubes. They analyzed the DNA of these tubes and discovered that they were the oesophagus of the urchin Carnarechinus clypeatus.

According to recent reports, “We were absolutely stunned to find this bivalve living inside the throat of a deepwater sea urchin,” Paul Valentich-Scott, a study co-author and marine malacologist at the Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History, said in a statement. “A Russian scientist [Alexander Mironov] originally thought these clams were being eaten by the sea urchin, but we later determined that it was actually living inside the oesophagus.”.

Mironov had noticed clams inside the urchin’s gut as far back as the 1970s and 1990s. The team also found related clams living inside of a specimen of the same urchin that was collected during the Challenger Expedition (1872 to 1876), where they had gone unnoticed for over a century.

In a recent development, most clam species that live with other animals cling to the outside of their host. Endocommensalism, or living inside of the host, is more rare. The fresh clam’s genus Vaticinaria is only the second clam genus of its superfamily known to live this way.

In a recent development, “Endocommensalism is extremely rare in galeommatids and all bivalves,” Valentich-Scott added. “Most commensal bivalves attach to the outside of their host. This new species lives inside its throat.”.

It has been revealed that this fresh clam highlights no obvious adaptations to life inside a host. It is about 0.74 inches long, which is large for its group, and has a shell that closes fully. The species name gulicola comes from the Latin word for “throat” and “inhabitant.” Much about the clam remains unknown and will require further study.

According to recent reports, “We know very little about this fresh species or its sea urchin host,” said Valentich-Scott. “The host sea urchin has never been collected intact, so we really don’t even know what it looks like. We have no idea how this bivalve can live inside the throat of the urchin, or what it eats.”.

Industry observers note that the team suspects that the clams can feed off the nutrient-rich sediment that the urchin eats, but this hasn’t been studied. Further deep-sea sampling should reveal more about this clam and other unusual creatures of the deep-sea.

Tesla FSD v15 is AI4’s last shot as Musk reveals how little compute is left

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars.
  • He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.
  • The most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars. Elon Musk spent the weekend explaining on X how the newly introduced software uses the hardware, and there isn’t much room left.

He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.

The most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns. Musk called it “real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator.”.

The fan accounts ran with that as a flex. But Musk’s follow-up posts tell a different story.

In a recent development, he explained that after Tesla moved a decoder into SRAM, “we only have half a TRIP out of three on SoC B, for this reality visualizer, so spent the compute as best we could.” In other words, half a TRIP is what was left over. He added that TRIP, Tesla’s neural accelerator, “basically only handles 8-bit int and has to run softmax in emulation mode in 28 steps.”.

In another post, Musk described Reality View as a roughly 1-billion-parameter diffusion model running off the same vision encoder features “that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions.” He admitted the visualization’s latency is “a bit high due to compute constraints.”.

In a recent development, that 3B figure is worth noting. Tesla talked up a 10x jump in FSD model size for over a year, first for v14 and then for v15. Musk didn’t say whether 3B covers the entire driving stack, but it’s nowhere near 10x.

Recent findings suggest that and Tesla’s own engineers aren’t describing a chip with lots of headroom. Dilreet Raju, who works on Tesla’s AI silicon, wrote that the hardest work of his life was co-designing the v15 vision encoder “to squeeze out the last few percents of MFU from AI4.” MFU is model FLOPs utilization, a measure of how much of the chip’s theoretical compute the model actually uses. Musk replied with a target emoji.

Industry observers note that when Tesla unveiled its FSD computer in 2019, the selling point was redundancy: two independent chips on one board, each with its own power and memory, so one could take over if the other failed. As we noted when Tesla started shipping the AI4.5 computer in Model Y in January, Tesla’s FSD computers have historically used two identical chips for exactly that reason.

It has been revealed that that’s what an unsupervised, Level 4 system needs. With nobody in the driver’s seat, a hardware fault can’t simply hand control back to a human. The car needs enough healthy compute left to keep seeing the road and pull over safely.

But Musk’s own description shows SoC B running the decoder and the Reality View model, not sitting idle as a mirror of SoC A. Tesla hackers, including greentheonly, have reported for years that Tesla started splitting its FSD workload across both chips back in the HW3 days.

Tesla has never explained how much of AI4 it reserves for failover, or whether a single SoC can run enough of the stack to bring a car to a safe stop on its own. The more of the board v15 needs, the harder that question gets.

Waymo has answered it publicly. The company says both of its onboard computing systems run full workloads in parallel and that a secondary computer can bring the vehicle to a safe stop if the primary fails, backed by redundant braking, steering and power. Its latest custom chip is rated at more than 1,000 TOPS. By our own comparison of AI4 and Nvidia’s Drive Thor, AI4 is estimated at roughly 100 to 150 TOPS across both chips.

It has been revealed that tesla started rolling out FSD v15 on Saturday, claiming “25x better handling of safety critical cases” without any baseline. So far, the people posting videos are mostly the usual crowd of Tesla-focused accounts that get early builds. Just hours before the rollout started, Musk wrote that v15 “goes to wide release next month.”.

The early clips are almost all about Reality View, the new parking spot selection, and the floating arrows. Those are UI features. They say very little about how many miles v15 can drive between critical interventions, which is the only number that matters for unsupervised driving.

According to recent reports, that brings us to AI4.5. On Tesla’s Q1 2026 earnings call, Musk announced an “AI4 Plus” with RAM doubled from 16GB to 32GB per chip, which raised the question of whether HW4 would follow HW3.

Sources indicate that this weekend, Musk stated “AI4.5 is a relatively small performance improvement that is mostly due to needing to upgrade RAM to LPDDR5X.” Hours later, he added: “RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints.”.

He also said that AI4 “costs twice as much now due to memory and storage price hikes.”.

In a recent development, so the mid-cycle refresh exists mainly because Tesla needs a newer memory type it can actually buy, not to unlock bigger models. If memory bandwidth is the bottleneck, as Musk keeps repeating, adding capacity doesn’t change much.

Asked by an owner on Sunday whether to wait for AI5 before upgrading from HW3, Musk answered: “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”.

An interesting comment, as it destroys one thing that HW3 owners were holding to: Tesla was delaying HW3 upgrades until it had AI5. Now, it’s clearly not the case and Tesla has no excuse not to upgrade HW3 cars.

Sources indicate that he described AI5 as “a gigantic improvement. Roughly 12X more compute,” and later as “roughly an order of magnitude hardware performance improvement, all things considered. Memory bandwidth is a constraint.” Last year, he stated that by some metrics AI5 would be 40 times better than AI4.

AI5 is also moving around. In October, Musk mentioned Tesla cut AI5’s RAM in half to 72GB to get enough volume for Optimus, then nudged it back up to 96GB a day later. AI6 was cut by a third, to 144GB of LPDDR6. When asked about AI6 this weekend, Musk replied with a chef’s kiss meme.

In a recent development, as we reported in July, Samsung’s Texas fab won’t reach AI5 volume production until the second half of 2027, nearly two years behind Musk’s original timeline. And that volume is now headed to robots and data centers, not cars.

According to recent reports, this is the situation for AI4 owners: v15 has to be the one. And we heard Elon Musk calling every FSD enhancement “the one” for the last decade.

Sources indicate that tesla’s own engineers are talking about squeezing the last few percent of utilization out of AI4. Musk describes a half-accelerator scrap of compute left for the visualizer. The AI4.5 refresh is a RAM swap that just got downsized, and AI5 isn’t coming to cars. If v15 can’t get to unsupervised driving on AI4, there’s no hardware escape hatch for the fleet.

Industry observers note that I seem to remember a couple of years ago Tesla released a big upgrade in November, only to encounter chip overheating problems the following summer. Now they are admitting that the old chip is running flat out, that means heat. Heat that they have to get rid of in cars that already are dealing with inadequate cooling.

We’ve seen this movie before. Tesla said HW3 was enough for unsupervised self-driving until it wasn’t, and those owners are still waiting on an answer about upgrades. AI4 owners paid for the same promise.

And even if v15 drives well, I want to know how Tesla handles a chip failure with nobody behind the wheel. That’s not optional for Level 4. If the stack needs both SoCs to drive, what brings the car to a safe stop when one of them crashes?

Sources indicate that as for v15 itself, I’m not drawing conclusions from influencer clips. Reality View looks great, but it’s also visibly laggy, and Musk admits it’s compute-limited. A great visual upgrade is nice. Driving performance is what matters. I’ll wait until I get it in my own car to see how significant the improvement actually is.

Can Pirelli’s Cyber Tyre Technology Replace Drive Modes?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout.
  • In a recent development, that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data.
  • It has been revealed that "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout. The tires use a sensor that looks a lot like a Dexcom G7 to feed temperature, air pressure, acceleration, and identification data to a vehicle's computers.

In a recent development, that information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data. For example, swap your summer tires for squishier winter rubber, and a compatible car could recognize the change and automatically adjust how its electronic controls intervene, leaving you free to imagine a world where maybe we all just drove better.

See all results for used cars for sale near 60629.

It has been revealed that "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani. The sensor, weighing just 13 grams, is bonded to the tire's inner liner beneath the tread using a specially developed adhesive and rubber housing. The process was developed using learnings from Pirelli's Noise Cancelling System, which uses foam inside the tire to absorb sound waves and reduce cabin vibration. The sensor must survive extreme temperatures, constant flexing, and the insane lateral g-forces that tires are susceptible to at over 200 mph. Engineers explained that its battery is designed to outlast the tire and enters a low-power sleep mode during extended storage.

Sources indicate that the more inspiring part is what the car does with the information it gathers. As we found in our recent all-weather tire comparison test, summer, winter, and all-season tires perform dramatically differently. Yet a vehicle's electronic controls are generally calibrated around its original equipment, using things like wheel speed sensors that aren’t as close to the road surface as the Cyber Tyre. Instead, it identifies the specific tire installed at each corner, allowing it to use different wheel-slip targets. And with the sensor attached to the inside of the tire, the data informing those systems is closer to the road surface than ever.

We sampled the technology at Las Vegas Motor Speedway in two Mercedes-AMG GT63 S four-doors wearing Cyber Tyre-equipped P Zero MS all-season tires.

Recent findings suggest that the first exercise had us pin the throttle through a corner from 40 mph using three different traction-control calibrations, all on the same P Zero MS all-season tires. The first, intended for ultra-high-performance summer tires, was overly restrictive, cutting power before the tires could deliver much acceleration. The second, calibrated for winter tires, permitted considerably more wheelspin, making the AMG easy to slide. Despite that setting being the most fun (and our favorite), Cyber Tyre delivered a happy medium, allowing more controlled acceleration without either extreme.

See all results for used cars for sale near 60629.

According to recent reports, this is where Cyber Tyre begins to make the case against selectable drive modes. The same car, wearing the same tires, just behaved three different ways without any mechanical changes. It's not going to replace the button that stiffens your dampers or changes your exhaust note, but it could eventually make some traction-related settings redundant.

In a recent development, the second AMG demonstrated ABS braking from 65 mph. With Cyber Tyre integration active, our stopping distance improved by 0.9 meter, or about three feet, according to Pirelli's instrumentation. That's not dramatically different, but still a measurable improvement.

Industry observers note that of course, these demonstrations weren't proof that Cyber Tyre can outperform a conventional system already calibrated for the correct tires. And the technology isn't smart enough to know it's snowing just because the tires are cold. But the distinction is that Cyber Tyre can give the car information about its tires without the driver doing anything. That could be super useful as tires wear, temperatures change, or owners swap between summer and winter sets. Pirelli is also developing tire-wear estimates using its sensor data, which could prove useful for fleet operators managing hundreds of vehicles.

It has been revealed that pirelli and Bosch confirmed their development partnership in 2024, and the technology has already appeared in vehicles from McLaren and Pagani. Pirelli executives say a substantially higher-volume application should be announced in the first half of 2027, with production expected in 2028. So it's possible this tech could arrive in models as common as a Ford pickup.

It has been revealed that pirelli is also investing approximately $1.2 billion to expand its Rome, Georgia, manufacturing facility, where Cyber Tyre-equipped products will be produced alongside conventional tires. By 2033, the firm expects annual production capacity to reach six million tires and intends to add up to 1000 engineering jobs.

In a recent development, they also recently unveiled that China's state-owned Sinochem, formerly Pirelli's largest shareholder, reduced its ownership to 13.6 percent in November. The Italian government has restricted Sinochem's influence and specifically prohibited sharing Cyber Tyre data with entities connected to the Chinese government. Following those governance changes, Pirelli received U.S. authorization to market the technology here. Not that anyone was worried about a Pagani Utopia Roadster being a boon of classified information.

Industry observers note that cyber Tyre isn't about to take the Ford Bronco's G.O.A.T. modes out back to shoot them. There are plenty of reasons to let drivers decide how their cars behave. But after experiencing three dramatically different calibrations in the same AMG, it's easy to see why some of those decisions might eventually be better left to the car. Just make sure we’re able to fully disable them.

Austin Irwin has worked for Car and Driver for over 10 years in various roles. He's steadily worked his way from an entry-level data entry position into driving vehicles for photography and video, and is now reviewing and testing cars. What will he do next? Who knows, but he better be fast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turkeys may be getting all of the bird hype this week, but plenty is still going on in the reality show that is the bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) world.

In a recent development, just before the sun rose over Big Bear Valley in southern California on Monday morning, Friends of Big Bear Valley’s (FOBBV) cameras picked up the sounds of eagle chortles throughout the area. The sounds continued as the sun came up over the nest that typically belongs to an internet-famous bald eagle dad named Shadow and his late partner, Jackie.

In a recent development, “Eagles vocalize for many different reasons. It could be to communicate territory, a danger warning, mating, food necessity or merely social contact. Their tone is that of a whistling chatter-like chirp, making it easy to differentiate them with their distinctive, high pitched sounds,” FOBBV writes.

Recent findings suggest that the cameras also picked up two unknown soaring eagles, and some ravens scrounging around in the nest. By Monday afternoon, two bald eagles followed each other onto the Lookout Snag, a tree near the nest. While it is not clear which eagles were there, a familiar face was spotted just before sunset. Kaydee, the four-year-old banded female eagle who has been seen near Shadow since August, swooped onto the nest for the first time in several days.

“Kaydee made a welcome visit to the nest. She poked around a bit, before showing us some beautiful closeups, then exiting through the back porch,” FOBBV says. “We can all agree what a welcome sight it was to see Kaydee. It’s a gentle reminder that if we just wait, there are upcoming surprises each and every day.”.

Recent findings suggest that we still do not know if Shadow and Kaydee will mate this season. Shadow has recently been spotted with another female eagle nicknamed Substantial Beautiful Visitor (BBV) by some fans. Any eggs are generally laid in January. Viewers can follow Shadow, Kaydee, or any other eagle couple that takes over the nest via a 24/7 livestream.

Recent findings suggest that kaydee, formerly known as KD1, is a banded female bald eagle that has been spotted in Big Bear Valley following the death of Shadow’s former partner, Jackie. She was born in 2022, about 70 miles away from Big Bear Lake in the Prado Basin between Anaheim and Riverside, California. Coincidentally, her parents are also named Lucky and Ricky like Jackie’s parents, but they are a different eagle pair.

Industry observers note that kaydee was banded as part of the Orange County Water District’s work to track the eagles born in the area. These bands help biologists track and monitor the birds over time. Kaydee currently has a black spot on her head, but that may not be permanent. It’s possible that not all of her white feathers have come in or it could be tree sap or dirt. She also has two small bands on her legs. One is a small metal band, while the other is a lavender band with “KD1” on it.

Kaydee is almost five years old, so she is just about ready to mate.

According to recent reports, in January, Jackie laid two eggs in the nest, but ravens destroyed them. She later laid two more eggs that hatched in April and named Luna and Sandy. The name Sandy is in honor of FOBBV’s former executive director Sandy Steers, who died from cancer in February.

On July 17, Jackie was found injured on the ground near Dana Point Park, California. Cell phone video from a witness confirmed that she had an altercation with two other subadult eagles. She successfully fended off the other eagles by turning over and using her talons, but could not fly far away.

Recent findings suggest that she was transferred to the Ojai Raptor Center for care, where she was diagnosed with severe anemia. Her anemia worsened during the first week of August, the Ojai Raptor Center mentioned that she was in unstable condition on August 9.

According to recent reports, jackie died early in the morning on August 10. The necropsy did not reveal a single cause of death, and instead pointed to several factors including severe anemia, bird flu, blood clots in her wing and one kidney, and liver and lung abnormalities.

A memorial service was held on September 5 in Fawnskin, California, along with a second celebration of life called Wings Over Major Bear on October 3. The event featured representatives from FOBBV, the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, and more.

Earlier this month, the Ojai Raptor Center announced a “room filled with kindness,” that is covered with thousands of letters, drawings, cards, and well-wishes they have received in honor of Jackie.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is overhauling its best-selling vehicle of all time, which will include the first fully electric Corolla.

The Toyota Corolla is one of the most recognized and best-selling automotive nameplates of all time.

Since its debut in 1966, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla thanks to its reliability, low cost of ownership, efficiency, and affordable price tag.

Toyota sells the Corolla in more than 150 countries and has expanded the lineup over the past 50 years from sedans and hatchbacks to coupes, wagons, a sporty GR Corolla, and the Corolla Cross compact SUV.

For its 13th generation, Toyota is planning a major overhaul that’s expected to be its biggest transformation yet.

The next-gen Toyota Corolla will be based on a fresh “multipathway” platform that will support gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and, for the first time, fully electric powertrains.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle ― whatever the power source ― let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s former president and current CEO Koji Sato said after unveiling the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Toyota has kept most details a secret, including battery and powertrain specs. However, the latest version is expected to adopt a similar design to the concept.

“When we created the concept, we wanted to give the Corolla name a newly introduced twist,” Norihiko Kobayashi, who has led the Corolla program since 2011, told Motor.es during a recent interview.

The Corolla has undergone several minor updates over the past 60 years, but the next-gen model will look nothing like its predecessors.

“It wasn’t simply about following in the footsteps of the past,” Kobayashi explained, “we wanted to delve into the future while still maintaining the Corolla identity.”.

Developing the next-gen Corolla “wasn’t just about making a upcoming car, but about redefining the future without looking back,” he added.

Like the current version, the latest Toyota Corolla will come in several different body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and a GR variant.

If they can deliver a Corolla cross EV for $30k sticker that dealers sell for $27k. That could be a large market a win for everyone . They appear to be doing what they did with hybrid and what KHG did with some models for a few years. Just starting with hybrid then going shades to pure bev.

Details have yet to be confirmed, but the Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations and offer a pure electric driving range of at least 250 miles.

The hybrid will reportedly use a newly introduced 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the hybrid system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Recent findings suggest that toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

#144093. Latest Update: 3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

Latest Update: 3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son.
  • The client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son. The text was just a photo of her son's dog wearing (or at least trying to wear) a cap of a major league baseball team. She said, "Dr. Jeff, it's been two months since I last heard from him, and of course, I immediately smiled when I saw the pic. But I had no idea what to do next." This client elaborated that her fingers led her to compose and immediately delete five responses prior to sending them. She added, "No matter what I do, he will pull away again, anyway.".

The client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child. She didn't know whether to joke about the cute picture, or tell her son she missed him, or ask further about Thanksgiving. For any parents in similar situations, it can be maddening to feel unsure about how to respond.

Sources indicate that and, if you have not spoken to your adult child for over six months or even years, the absence of that relationship has a huge, seemingly constant presence. By this I mean that often in these partial or full-on estrangement situations, the reality is that minimal or no contact does not take away from the internal emotional upheaval that comes from the desire to reconnect.

Recent findings suggest that it is easy to feel helpless in the face of not seeing your adult child or not having the level of connection that you value. In my parent coaching work, I encourage parents to focus on three things they can do no matter how long it's been since they last heard their grown child's voice.

According to recent reports, finish this sentence: "What I miss most about my grown child today is__________." Some parents might reply that they wish they knew how their son was doing. Maybe, as in the early example of the dog photo, a parent misses lighter moments of laughter. Maybe a song reminds you of your adult child.

Identifying what you miss is tangible and healthy because it helps you process difficult feelings like sadness, disappointment, nostalgia, or loneliness. For example, that treasured memory of you and your daughter going for a ride and belting out a shared favorite song may weigh heavily on your mind. Consider sharing these thoughts with trusted relatives, friends, a therapist, or a parent coach. Sometimes it helps to have someone just say, "Tell me more.".

Consider your adult daughter saying to you, "When I tell you what bothered me that you did when I was growing up, you kept twisting it to make it my fault and giving me advice." You may remember trying to help. But hold on, because, at the same time, maybe you can recall trying to give her advice when she stated, "Dad, can I finish my point?".

Looking at your own behaviors in this way gives you an honest point of reflection to start. You could then say, "I've been reflecting on times I rushed in to give you advice, and it got in the way of better understanding what you were going through, and I'm sorry." This type of dialogue not only highlights that you are taking responsibility, but you are also modeling self-awareness to your adult child.

In my book, You Ruined My Life—Now You Owe Me!, I explore how easily a parent's regret can turn into a feeling of indebtedness. In the parent coaching trenches, I have seen how tempting it is for parents to promise their adult children something to bring them closer. Please keep in mind that you can offer a sincere apology and still take your time to decide what you can reasonably do or give. For parents who are totally out of contact, I suggest you write down what you regret and keep it private.

This third point is really hard for parents missing their adult children. If several messages go unanswered, give your adult child room to reach out. If they asked for no contact, honor that request. Believe it or not, adult children in these situations often share with me that they still love and even miss their parents, even when they outwardly state they want no contact. Just remember what I wrote above: The absence of contact still has a great presence in both your mind and that of your adult child.

Bose kept the 12-hour battery from the original and added AAC and aptX Adaptive support, so both iPhone and Android owners get a better Bluetooth connection than the first model’s SBC-only setup. A customizable shortcut button handles tasks like pairing a second speaker. At $99, it grabs your attention for more than sonic reasons. Alternately, the Marshall Emberton III is a palm-sized powerhouse at $89.99 (was $179.99), and its amp-inspired design is rated IP67 against dust and water. For a bigger sound at a backyard party, the Sony ULT Field 5 falls to $188 (was $349.99) … and the bigger, punchier ULT Tower 5 is $299. Those are just two of the two dozen amazing options listed below.

Sources indicate that the beyerdynamic DT 770 Pro has been a fixture in recording studios since the mid-1980s, and it works just as well for everyday listening at home. The closed-back design keeps outside noise out and your music in, while the plush velour pads stay comfortable through long sessions. The 80-ohm version runs fine from a laptop or phone, though one of the DACs below will give it more headroom, making them a great buy at $139.99.

According to recent reports, the beyerdynamic DT 990 Pro is the open-back sibling of the DT 770 Pro above, and it drops to $139.99 (was $199.99). On the in-ear side, the 7Hz x Crinacle Zero:2 remain one of the best ways to hear what wired IEMs can do for about $21. Our list of the best mixing headphones can give you more studio insight.

A one-button turntable that plays nice with Bluetooth speakers and real stereos.

Sources indicate that if the PS-LX3BT above leaves you wanting more, the Sony PS-LX5BT is Sony’s step-up model with more premium components but still a nice price at $398 (was $499.99). According to recent reports, want to go digital? There are a ton of smart, whole-home, streaming-friendly connected speakers on sale below. We love a compact listening station.

The 61 Best New Reveals of 2026 (and 1 More We Can't Wait For)
